item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Ukraine has resumed missile strikes on Russian oil refineries and a missile-maintenance base, while the UK is sending additional Storm Shadow missiles for further attacks on Russia. Russian drones have attacked ships in the Black Sea near Romania, leaving seven crew members missing, and have disrupted health supply shipments in Ukraine. Kyiv blames SpaceX for throttling Starlink terminals that support its drone operations. Russia has detained a Japanese journalist on espionage charges. The conflict caused 75,767 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Israel, Gaza and the West Bank: the situation
item.description:
Israel has stopped commercial goods from entering Gaza while Hamas denies tax allegations, and Israeli forces killed a Palestinian woman in Gaza City and rescued a girl from a burning apartment. Iran saw two container ships sink near the Strait of Hormuz amid a surge in Iranian attacks, a development linked to the broader regional tension over Gaza. Azerbaijan hosted a rare summit that brought together both converging and opposing Middle East and Asian leaders, including Israeli and Palestinian representatives. The UCDP recorded 21,440 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Iran and the regional confrontation: the situation
item.description:
Houthi missiles have struck Yemen's presidential palace in Aden, killing five officials, and have also hit Saudi-led forces headquarters there and a Saudi airport, prompting Saudi air strikes on Houthi positions in Yemen. Iran has sunk two container ships in the Strait of Hormuz, increasing the threat to regional shipping, and its precision strikes have damaged Gulf infrastructure. Saudi diplomats say Iran is encouraging Houthi escalation against the kingdom. US officials are reportedly weighing the use of the "mother of all bombs" if fighting resumes. The conflict recorded 123 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

The attacks were part of a broader pattern of Houthi targeting of Saudi coalition command centres in the city. Simultaneously, migrants continue risking sea journeys to reach Yemen, while a besieged Yemeni city faces severe food and fuel shortages as Houthis press forward. The conflict produced 918 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Iraq: the situation
item.description:
Iraq's parliament has appointed US-sanctioned Laith al-Khazali as deputy prime minister, signaling continued political influence of sanctioned figures. Iraqi authorities have publicly pledged that Iraqi territory will not be used for attacks on Saudi Arabia, while Kataib Hezbollah warned it will target hostile aircraft over Iraq. Security forces have dismantled two human-trafficking networks, rescuing newborns, and foiled a ring selling infants. ISIS activity appears to be regrouping in Iraq following the US withdrawal. The conflict recorded 396 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Sudan's civil war: the situation
item.description:
The Sudanese Armed Forces have launched air strikes on gold mining sites near the Sudan-Egypt border, killing dozens of miners, while the Rapid Support Forces used a paramilitary drone to strike near the Ethiopian frontier, causing civilian casualties in West Kordofan. In the Blue Nile, the Sudanese army repelled a joint RSF and SPLM-N attack, inflicting heavy losses on the attackers. Doctors in Sudan report worsening detention conditions for more than 6,500 people held by the RSF. The conflict produced 4,680 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: South Sudan: the situation
item.description:
Communal clashes have intensified in Lakes state, especially around Rumbek, prompting curfews and a visit by caretaker governor Rin Tueny. UNMISS has stepped up civilian protection after deadly attacks in Rumbek, while SSPDF soldiers were wounded in an assault on a Mundri West military outpost and the U.S. Embassy condemned an assault on WFP workers in Jonglei that involved looting of aid. An AIC cleric was shot dead in Juba and a Juba High Court sentenced five officers to 24 years for raiding a general's home. The lethal communal violence now far exceeds the two battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Ethiopia: the situation
item.description:
Ethiopian forces have captured a key town in Tigray along with its regional airport and are advancing toward an Eritrean border town, while intense fighting in Amhara has left at least 183 dead, according to the UN. The United States has increased diplomatic pressure, urging Ethiopia and Eritrea to de-escalate as the conflict spreads. Leaders of Egypt, Eritrea, Sudan and Somalia are meeting to coordinate security operations if the fighting crosses borders. The war caused 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:

Islamist fighters attacked a Borno military base, killing soldiers, and ISWAP also struck a base, causing further casualties. A Nigerian who allegedly cooked for unknown gunmen is heading to the US Supreme Court for an asylum review. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Somalia: the situation
item.description:

The Somali government is screening travelers after Kenya confirmed an imported Ebola case and is hosting regional talks in Egypt with Eritrea, Sudan and its own officials to coordinate security amid rising Ethiopia-Eritrea tensions. The federal government is deepening defence ties with Pakistan, seeking JF‑17 fighter jets and securing the release of four Pakistani sailors freed from Somali pirates. item.title: The Sahel insurgency: the situation
item.description:
Gunmen attacked an immigration patrol in Niger State, killing one officer and wounding another, and also burned the officer's body. Bandits carried out a separate assault in Borgu LGA, while a Christian humanitarian worker was slain in northwest Nigeria and a Niger lawyer was jailed for a social-media post about the army. The United States added Nigeria to its blacklist for recruiting child soldiers, and Mali expanded its reserve force by 2,400 recruits, including 800 women. These incidents show a widening of violence beyond isolated attacks on security forces to include civilian targets and legal repression. Erik Prince is operating a private mercenary effort targeting the gangs. The United Nations has allocated an additional US$75 million for life-saving aid to 507,000 people and renewed sanctions on Haiti for another year. item.title: Colombia: the situation
